images.title: Zeroes match decimal places
images.purpose: Recap the topic: the number of zeroes in the denominator equals the number of digits after the decimal point.
images.composition: A compact 3 row table sits in the centre with a matching count tag on the right of each row; white space around it.
exact_structure: One table of 3 rows, centred, each row a fraction, an equals sign and a decimal.
Row 1: "37/10 = 3.7", the 1 zero in the denominator in teal #0072B2 and the 1 digit after the point (7) in teal #0072B2; tag on the right "1 place".
Row 2: "37/100 = 0.37", the 2 zeroes in the denominator in amber #E69F00 and the 2 digits after the point (3 and 7) in amber #E69F00; tag "2 places".
Row 3: "37/1000 = 0.037", the 3 zeroes in the denominator in reddish purple #CC79A7 and the 3 digits after the point (0, 3 and 7) in reddish purple #CC79A7; tag "3 places".
Thin grey #6B7280 lines separate the rows; nothing else in the frame.
rejection: the count of coloured zeroes in a denominator differing from the count of coloured digits after the point in its row
images.takeaway: Count the zeroes in the denominator to know how many digits come after the point.
images.description: A three row table showing 37/10 = 3.7, 37/100 = 0.37 and 37/1000 = 0.037, with matching colours for the zeroes and the digits after the point, tagged 1, 2 and 3 places.
images.context: Shown beside the practice concept as a quick recap of the topic before the questions.
images.teaching_notes: Match each coloured zero in a denominator with a coloured digit after the point in the same row.

image_decisions.why: A compact recap visual of the zero counting idea helps students before they practise.
